COC-ANALYSIS-REPORT.DOCX
CHANGE OF CONTROL AND ASSIGNMENT PROVISION ANALYSIS — COMPREHENSIVE DEAL TEAM REPORT

CORPORATE M&A — DUE DILIGENCE / COUNTERPARTY MARKUP RECONCILIATION
Acquisition Data Room Materials Review

=====================================================================
I. SCOPE AND PURPOSE
=====================================================================

This report to the deal team analyzes the change of control ("COC") and assignment provisions appearing across the target's material contracts, reconciles the counterparty's latest markup of the operative contracting documentation against the base acquisition data room materials, and recommends responses for each deviation introduced. The deliverable is prepared for the corporate M&A engagement analyzing change of control provisions across the target's material contracts (Due Diligence Report).

The analysis is based on the following matter documents, all read in full:
  • Matter engagement file (input materials) — sets the scope, key provisions framework, and required output.
  • Counterparty markup — the counterparty's latest revision to the operative agreement, introducing deviations that must be reconciled to the base materials.
  • Schedules and exhibits — disclosure schedules qualifying the base materials, including Schedule 3.7, Schedule 5.2, and Exhibit B, which control over general statements in the base materials.
  • Deal team correspondence — the partner email thread on this engagement, the latest message of which controls the analysis priorities.

The misfiled administrative correspondence for this matter folder (administrative file 8) concerns an unrelated client engagement and is expressly excluded from reliance in this report.

=====================================================================
II. THE BASE DATA ROOM MATERIALS — CHANGE OF CONTROL AND ASSIGNMENT
=====================================================================

The acquisition data room base materials set the benchmark against which every counterparty revision is measured. For purposes of this report, the operative base positions on the two subject areas in the target's material contracts are as follows:

A. Change of Control Provisions
The base materials establish that, where a change of control provision applies to a material contract of the target, the following structure governs:
  • A "change of control" is defined to encompass a merger, a sale of a majority of the equity or voting securities, and a sale of all or substantially all of the assets of the subject entity.
  • The change of control clause operates as a notification-and-termination provision: the counterparty must give the non-affected party prompt written notice of any covered change of control, and the non-affected party may terminate the contract within a defined notice window (typically ninety days) after receiving that notice.
  • The change of control rights are contract-specific and arise only where the contract expressly so states; the base materials do not impute a COC termination right to every contract.
  • A change of control is generally treated as distinct from an assignment (see below); the base structure does not automatically recharacterize a COC as a prohibited assignment, and does not require consent for a COC of a party solely on that basis.

B. Assignment Provisions
The base data room materials reflect a persistent prohibition on assignment without prior written consent:
  • Neither party may assign the contract, in whole or in part, without the prior written consent of the other party.
  • A change of control of a party (whether by merger or by sale of stock) is expressly NOT deemed an assignment under the base formulation, requires no consent or notice, and gives the other party no termination right.
  • Certain license-type contracts may impose a stricter bar, prohibiting assignment, transfer, or sublicense without prior written consent and characterizing the license as personal to the licensee.
  • Because the base materials separate the COC analysis from the assignment analysis, a reviewing party must test each material contract on its own terms, verifying (i) whether a COC triggers a termination right and (ii) whether a change of control would be treated as a prohibited assignment.

=====================================================================
III. THE COUNTERPARTY MARKUP — DEVIATIONS IDENTIFIED
=====================================================================

The counterparty's revision accepts most firm-standard provisions, but introduces three categories of deviation that must be reconciled against the base materials before the deliverable is finalized.

Deviation 1 — Indemnification Cap Reduction and Basket Conversion
The markup silently reduces the indemnification cap applicable to the operative agreement and converts the recovery basket from a true deductible into a tipping (first-dollar) basket. Under the base materials, the cap is a negotiated ceiling (in the relevant precedent, ten percent of purchase price), and the basket operates as a true deductible — the indemnitor is liable only for losses in excess of the threshold and not for the threshold itself. The counterparty markup (i) lowers the cap and (ii) converts the mechanism so that once the threshold is crossed the indemnitor is liable from the first dollar.

Reconciliation: This deviation is cumulative and materially adverse to the client. The cap reduction and basket flip together expand the client's exposure band on both the vertical axis (lower ceiling) and the horizontal axis (first-dollar recovery). It must be flagged as a markup item requiring a response.

Deviation 2 — Material Adverse Effect ("MAE") Carve-Outs
The markup's definition of Material Adverse Effect adds carve-outs for regulatory action of exactly the kind at issue in this matter. The base definition excludes or does not otherwise identify these categories as MAE exceptions; the counterparty seeks to isolate them so that they do not constitute (or contribute to) a Material Adverse Effect.

Reconciliation: This deviation intersects directly with the disclosure schedules. Schedule 3.7 of the schedule exhibit discloses two pending regulatory inquiries against the target. The counterparty's proposed carve-outs would exclude the consequences of those very inquiries from the MAE analysis.
